accepted.name: hcpcs_canonical
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  HCPC AS hcpcs_code,
  SAFE_CAST(RECID AS INT64) AS recid,
  SEQNUM AS seqnum,
  LONG_DESCRIPTION AS long_description,
  SHORT_DESCRIPTION AS short_description,
  PRICE1 AS price1_raw,
  PRICE2 AS price2_raw,
  PRICE3 AS price3_raw,
  PRICE4 AS price4_raw,
  SAFE_CAST(MCM1 AS FLOAT64) AS mcm1,
  SAFE_CAST(MCM2 AS INT64) AS mcm2,
  STATUTE AS statute,
  COV AS coverage_indicator,
  ASC_GRP AS asc_group,
  ADD_DT AS add_date,
  ACT_EFF_DT AS active_effective_date,
  TERM_DT AS termination_date,
  ACTION_CD AS action_active_flag
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.hcpcs`
grain: hcpcs_code, recid  -- one row per HCPCS code version (RECID)
accepted.description: Canonicalized HCPCS code dimension: one row per HCPC+RECID with cleaned, consistently-named columns and parsed numeric measures. Use when joining HCPCS metadata to utilization facts or when filtering by HCPCS attributes. | Use for: Look up HCPCS descriptions for codes in utilization data; Filter HCPCS codes by effective/termination date or coverage flag; Aggregate utilization by HCPCS metadata fields (asc_group, statute)

accepted.name: physicians_top_hcpcs_rank_per_provider_year
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  npi,
  hcpcs_code,
  SAFE_CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS year,
  line_srvc_cnt,
  bene_unique_cnt,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY npi, SAFE_CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) ORDER BY SAFE_CAST(line_srvc_cnt AS FLOAT64) DESC) AS rank_by_line_srvc_cnt
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2012' AND '2015'
grain: npi, hcpcs_code, year  -- one row per provider-HCPCS-year with rank within provider-year
accepted.description: Per-provider-per-year HCPCS ranking by line service count. Exposes rank so callers can filter to top-K procedures per provider per year. Use for top-K analyses of which HCPCS each provider billed most frequently. | Use for: Select top-N HCPCS per provider in a given year by service count; Compare top billed procedures across providers or states; Examine beneficiary counts for top procedures

accepted.name: physicians_utilization_hcpcs_joined
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.npi AS npi,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS year,
  p.hcpcs_code AS hcpcs_code,
  p.hcpcs_description AS hcpcs_description_fact,
  h.SHORT_DESCRIPTION AS hcpcs_short_description_dim,
  h.LONG_DESCRIPTION AS hcpcs_long_description_dim,
  p.line_srvc_cnt AS line_srvc_cnt,
  p.bene_unique_cnt AS bene_unique_cnt,
  p.average_medicare_payment_amt AS avg_medicare_payment_amt,
  p.average_medicare_allowed_amt AS avg_medicare_allowed_amt,
  p.nppes_provider_state AS provider_state,
  p.place_of_service AS place_of_service,
  h.COV AS coverage_indicator,
  h.MCM1 AS mcm1
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*` AS p
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.hcpcs` AS h
  ON p.hcpcs_code = h.HCPC
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2012' AND '2015'
grain: npi, hcpcs_code, year  -- denormalized provider-HCPCS-year row
accepted.description: Denormalized view joining physician utilization facts to HCPCS canonical dimension. Preserves provider, hcpcs, year and exposes both utilization measures and HCPCS metadata for filtering and grouping. | Use for: Assess payment differences by HCPCS attributes; Filter utilization by HCPCS coverage or metadata; Rank HCPCS within providers using enriched metadata

accepted.name: hospice_providers_2014_race_gender_share_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id AS provider_id,
  name AS provider_name,
  state AS provider_state,
  hospice_beneficiaries AS hospice_beneficiaries,
  IFNULL(male_hospice_beneficiaries,0) AS male_beneficiaries,
  IFNULL(female_hospice_beneficiaries,0) AS female_beneficiaries,
  IFNULL(white_hospice_beneficiaries,0) AS white_beneficiaries,
  IFNULL(black_hospice_beneficiaries,0) AS black_beneficiaries,
  IFNULL(asian_hospice_beneficiaries,0) AS asian_beneficiaries,
  IFNULL(hispanic_hospice_beneficiaries,0) AS hispanic_beneficiaries,
  IFNULL(other_unknown_race_hospice_beneficiaries,0) AS other_unknown_race_beneficiaries,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(IFNULL(male_hospice_beneficiaries,0), NULLIF(hospice_beneficiaries,0)) AS share_male,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(IFNULL(female_hospice_beneficiaries,0), NULLIF(hospice_beneficiaries,0)) AS share_female,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(IFNULL(white_hospice_beneficiaries,0), NULLIF(hospice_beneficiaries,0)) AS share_white,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(IFNULL(black_hospice_beneficiaries,0), NULLIF(hospice_beneficiaries,0)) AS share_black,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(IFNULL(asian_hospice_beneficiaries,0), NULLIF(hospice_beneficiaries,0)) AS share_asian,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(IFNULL(hispanic_hospice_beneficiaries,0), NULLIF(hospice_beneficiaries,0)) AS share_hispanic,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(IFNULL(other_unknown_race_hospice_beneficiaries,0), NULLIF(hospice_beneficiaries,0)) AS share_other_unknown,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY hospice_beneficiaries DESC) AS rank_within_state,

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.hospice_providers_2014`

accepted.description: Compute race and gender shares and rank providers by hospice_beneficiaries within their state and overall. accepted.name: person_event_counts_by_domain
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.person_id,
  COALESCE(obs.observation_count, 0) AS observation_count,
  COALESCE(drug.drug_exposure_count, 0) AS drug_exposure_count,
  COALESCE(cond.condition_occurrence_count, 0) AS condition_occurrence_count,
  COALESCE(proc.procedure_occurrence_count, 0) AS procedure_occurrence_count,
  COALESCE(dev.device_exposure_count, 0) AS device_exposure_count,
  (COALESCE(obs.observation_count, 0)
   + COALESCE(drug.drug_exposure_count, 0)
   + COALESCE(cond.condition_occurrence_count, 0)
   + COALESCE(proc.procedure_occurrence_count, 0)
   + COALESCE(dev.device_exposure_count, 0)) AS total_event_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` AS p
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(1) AS observation_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation`
  GROUP BY person_id
) AS obs
ON p.person_id = obs.person_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(1) AS drug_exposure_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure`
  GROUP BY person_id
) AS drug
ON p.person_id = drug.person_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(1) AS condition_occurrence_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.condition_occurrence`
  GROUP BY person_id
) AS cond
ON p.person_id = cond.person_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(1) AS procedure_occurrence_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.procedure_occurrence`
  GROUP BY person_id
) AS proc
ON p.person_id = proc.person_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(1) AS device_exposure_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.device_exposure`
  GROUP BY person_id
) AS dev
ON p.person_id = dev.person_id
grain: person_id -- one row per person with aggregated event counts
accepted.description: Per-person counts of key event types (observations, drug_exposures, condition_occurrences, procedure_occurrences, device_exposures). accepted.name: observations_latest_per_person_concept_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  observation_id,
  person_id,
  observation_concept_id,
  observation_date,
  observation_datetime,
  observation_type_concept_id,
  value_as_number,
  value_as_string,
  value_as_concept_id,
  qualifier_concept_id,
  unit_concept_id,
  provider_id,
  visit_occurrence_id,
  visit_detail_id,
  observation_source_value,
  observation_source_concept_id,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY person_id, observation_concept_id ORDER BY COALESCE(observation_datetime, CAST(observation_date AS DATETIME)) DESC, observation_id DESC) AS rank_within_person_concept
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation`
